key_insight: Federated learning across LEO orbital planes, coordinated via HAPS, enables distributed, privacy-preserving beam selection using compact MLP/GNN models—delivering robust beam management under highly dynamic propagation without central raw-data exchange.
problem_solved: Efficient, scalable beam selection for LEO non-terrestrial networks where centralized training is impractical due to latency, limited fronthaul, and heterogeneous dynamic channels across satellites.
method: Federated learning architecture: orbital planes act as distributed learners; HAPS nodes coordinate local model aggregation without sharing raw channel data.
Modeling and comparison: train lightweight MLP and topology-aware GNN models locally on realistic channel and beamforming datasets, aggregate updates via FL rounds.
Evaluation with realistic simulations: measure beam-selection accuracy, convergence behavior, communication overhead and robustness to dynamic orbital/channel conditions.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for bringing ML into 6G NTN beam management—reducing backhaul needs and preserving data locality—while showing how model choice (MLP vs GNN) trades off complexity and topology-awareness for practitioners designing distributed radio-intelligence.
visual_elements: System diagram showing LEO satellites (orbital planes) as FL clients, HAPS as aggregation/coordination hub, and ground users/beams.
Comparative model block: compact MLP vs topology-aware GNN with callouts on suitability (compute, topology use).
Performance chart(s): beam-selection accuracy and communication overhead per FL round (relative comparison, e.g., MLP vs GNN vs centralized baseline).
Sequence/timeline visualization of beam dynamics and FL rounds illustrating robustness to channel changes and low raw-data exchange.
paper_title: Federated Learning-driven Beam Management in LEO 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks
paper_authors: Maria Lamprini Bartsioka, Ioannis A. Bartsiokas, Athanasios D. Panagopoulos, Dimitra I. Kaklamani, Iakovos S. Venieris
